purpose: Literature-based theoretical nominations for the contest. Evidence of completed experimental rescue is not an eligibility prerequisite. These nominations complement the broad screen; ranks are qualitative research judgments, not calibrated probabilities.
ranking_scope: Protein restoration and selected downstream mechanisms researched by this agent; other team research on phenylbutyrate and mTOR may outrank these in the combined shortlist.

evidence_chain: North et al. directly showed that SIRT2 deacetylates BUBR1 K668, reducing ubiquitination/proteasomal degradation; NMN increased BUBR1 abundance, and genetic SIRT2 overexpression extended lifespan in male BubR1-hypomorphic mice.
Pirinen et al. directly showed that nicotinic acid raises blood NAD+ and restores low muscle NAD+ in adults with mitochondrial myopathy.
Inference: approved nicotinic acid could substitute as an upstream NAD+ booster and preserve residual functional BUBR1. The drug-to-BUBR1 link is inferred across studies, not measured in MVA.

approval.indication: Specified lipid disorders and related indications

contradictions_and_dependencies: Nicotinamide is chemically distinct: in the North study it reduced BUBR1 under the tested sirtuin-inhibitory cell conditions. Do not substitute niacinamide or label all vitamin B3 forms equivalent.
Stabilization requires a residual protein substrate with useful function; it does not replace a missing C-terminal domain or repair a functionally defective stable mutant.
North's SIRT2-transgenic lifespan benefit was sex-dependent; small size and many senescence phenotypes persisted. NMN treatment and SIRT2 transgenic lifespan experiments were different interventions.
SIRT2 also deacetylates BUBR1 K250 in another primary study, with different cell-cycle consequences. K668 stabilization alone is an incomplete description of total SIRT2 action.

NAD+ elevation may be limited by tissue precursor metabolism or a nonlimiting starting NAD+ pool. Prescription ER formulation has a different exposure profile from the niacin preparation in the mitochondrial-myopathy study.

screen_context.interpretation: weak and mixed descriptive support, not a nomination gate

leads.discriminating_prediction: A residual-protein kinetic model predicts benefit increasing with residual synthesis and decreasing with NAD+ saturation; no abundance rescue when synthesis is zero. Model K668 stabilization separately from checkpoint timing, and compare NAD salvage/pathway expression across public proxy cells. Direct niacin-to-BUBR1 docking would not test this mechanism.

evidence_chain: Aminoglycoside action can permit near-cognate tRNA incorporation at premature stops.
Malik et al. measured heterogeneous dystrophin increases in a small human nonsense-mutation DMD study.
Inference: a BUB1B nonsense transcript that survives NMD could yield a longer protein with useful checkpoint function after readthrough.
contradictions_and_dependencies: RNA depletion, non-native residue incorporation and cytosolic exposure can limit useful product.
Sequence context matters and human DMD study did not establish simple stop-codon or +4-base rules.
Do not use the retracted 2017 gentamicin-B1 paper (PMID 28289221) as positive support.
leads.discriminating_prediction: Rank the actual local stop context against published reporter sequences; model residual transcript times readthrough rate times functional fraction. Compare structures of plausible readthrough amino-acid products and use ribosome-targeted simulations only with a credible molecular model.

evidence_chain: Baker et al. showed that eliminating senescent cells in BubR1-hypomorphic mice delayed tissue dysfunction.
Xu et al. showed JAK1/2 inhibition with ruxolitinib suppresses inflammatory SASP and improves physical function in naturally aged mice.
Inference: JAK1/2 inhibition could attenuate an inflammatory consequence of BUBR1 insufficiency, without correcting chromosome segregation.
contradictions_and_dependencies: Xu's mice were naturally aged, not BUB1B mutant; senescent-cell abundance did not significantly change.
Reduced inflammation is useful only if this downstream program is active; immune suppression and cytopenias oppose some intended benefits.
The evidence matrix maps S-ruxolitinib to the same parent; the stereoisomer requires exclusion or explicit identity resolution before pooling with the approved R drug.
leads.discriminating_prediction: Test signed IL6/JAK/STAT/SASP module reversal independently of proliferation and cell-death modules. Known JAK binding can anchor structural controls; BUBR1 binding is unnecessary for this mechanism.

evidence_chain: Nago et al. found oxidative stress in Sod1-deficient mouse oocytes accompanied reduced kinetochore BUBR1 and segregation errors.
NAC reduced segregation errors in that model.
Inference: reducing oxidative stress may prevent additional checkpoint impairment on top of BUB1B loss, without replacing BUBR1.
contradictions_and_dependencies: Evidence is a Sod1-deficient meiotic model exposed to culture oxidative stress, not congenital BUB1B-deficient mitosis.
Protection of a residual checkpoint cannot supply an absent core checkpoint component; antioxidant effects on malignant cells require a separate endpoint.
leads.discriminating_prediction: Stratify public BUB1B proxy signatures by oxidative-stress and glutathione modules and predict benefit only in the high-oxidative-stress subgroup; compare segregation endpoints to general viability.

leads.rationale: Retain an approved mechanistically distinct readthrough comparator, below gentamicin for direct readthrough evidence; better tolerability does not establish better rescue.
contradictions_and_dependencies: The later PCD reporter study found modest context-dependent effects and potential normalization artifacts.
Broad-screen same-cell score is essentially zero and chemical source identifiers are unresolved; neither establishes nor rules out local readthrough.
leads.discriminating_prediction: Use the same stop-context and product-function analysis as gentamicin, with a separate model for macrolide exposure and mechanism.

exclusion_or_direction_notes.reason: Suijkerbuijk2010 found HSP90 inhibition destabilized selected MVA BUBR1 mutants, opposing residual-protein rescue.
p53/p21 loss shortened lifespan and worsened muscle/fat deterioration in BubR1-hypomorphic mice. Suppressing every senescence-associated transcript is not a favorable signed intervention.

The p21 primary paper reports preliminary unpublished observations that rapamycin-fed BubR1 progeroid mice developed age-related phenotypes at similar rates to controls. This is pertinent negative evidence, with limited methodological detail, to weigh against specific mTOR-muscle evidence.

A primary high-dose culture study reports SAC deregulation and genotoxicity under low-glucose conditions. This is a context-specific adverse-direction result rather than a blanket conclusion at all exposures.
